result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_cosine_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get cosine similarity between all node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16189-L16241){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_cosine_similarity() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Cosine similarity](/assets/graphs/get-cosine-similarity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Nodes B and E are outlined in the accent color with their shared neighbors C and D filled in accent. The card divides the 2 shared neighbors by the square root of 3 times 4, about 3.464: cosine similarity 0.577." width="100%"} Cosine similarity treats neighbors as vector components: `Cosine(A, B) = |neighbors(A) ∩ neighbors(B)| / √(|neighbors(A)| × |neighbors(B)|)` Range: `[0, 1]` where `0` means no common neighbors and `1` means identical neighborhoods. Geometric interpretation: cosine of angle between neighbor vectors. Self-similarity is always `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nested dictionary mapping node IDs to dictionaries of similarity scores. Format: `{node1_id: {node2_id: similarity_score}}`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Treating each neighborhood as a $0/1$ indicator vector over the node set makes cosine similarity the angle between two such vectors: $\cos(\theta) = \dfrac{|N(u) \cap N(v)|}{\sqrt{|N(u)| \cdot |N(v)|}}$. The square root in the denominator is what makes it robust to degree imbalance where Jaccard's linear denominator would penalize high-degree nodes more heavily. That property, together with the direct interpretability as an angle, is why cosine has become the standard similarity in text mining (over tf-idf vectors), recommendation systems (user-item overlap), and graph embeddings alike. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a triangle, every node shares exactly one neighbor with each of the others, so cosine similarity works out to `1 / sqrt(2 * 2) = 0.5` for every pair: ::: {#6e6cba32 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) sim = graph.get_cosine_similarity() a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") sim[a_id][b_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.4999999999999999 ``` ::: :::
